reality.qualifier: MotorTrend Road-Trip Range Test on 2023 Ioniq 6 SE RWD measured 291 mi at constant 70 mph using 95% of full charge. SuperChevy long-term test confirmed similar real-world range during 1,200 mile road trip — '2024 Hyundai Ioniq 6's EPA-Estimated 361-Mile Range Remains Out of Reach.'
reality.verbatim_quote: we were able to eke out 291 miles at a constant 70 mph using 95 percent of a full charge in our MotorTrend Road Trip Range test… the day-to-day reality is always more complicated.

sources.name: SuperChevy / MotorTrend — Hyundai Ioniq 6 Yearlong Review (range test)

narrative_one_liner: Ioniq 6 SE RWD LR 361 mi EPA; MotorTrend 70 mph test 291 mi (-19%) — a 70-mile shortfall on the 'efficiency leader' sedan.
narrative: Hyundai advertises 361 mi EPA combined for the Ioniq 6 SE RWD Long Range — Hyundai's claimed EV efficiency leader. MotorTrend's instrumented 70 mph Road-Trip Range Test (using 95% of battery capacity) measured 291 miles, a 70-mile, 19% shortfall. SuperChevy's long-term real-world test concurred: 'the 2024 Hyundai Ioniq 6's EPA-Estimated 361-Mile Range Remains Out of Reach.' This is among the larger negative gaps in the Phase 1 dataset.
methodology_notes: MotorTrend's 95% capacity protocol is more conservative than running to dashboard zero. SuperChevy's long-term test is real-world rather than steady-state but confirms the directional finding.
caveats: Single primary Tier-2 instrumented source (MotorTrend); SuperChevy provides corroboration but at a lower methodological standard.
MotorTrend tested 2023 model; product record is 2025. Hardware platform unchanged per EPA filings.
Hyundai's claim that the Ioniq 6 is an efficiency leader is partly true: it is Hyundai's most efficient EV, but it does not deliver its EPA number at highway speed.
alternative_explanations: Aero-optimized streamliner shape gives Ioniq 6 the lowest drag coefficient (0.21) among Hyundai EVs, so the gap is not aero-related.
EPA test cycle's lower average speeds favor the sedan's regenerative-braking-heavy efficiency profile vs steady-state highway.
